page.layout: One page of running text, in one column. Running head with page number at the top (Greek running title left, page number 29 right). Below the first block of prose, a blank gap, then a set of italic Latin paragraphs. Gathering signature "C 3" at the lower left, and a number at the lower right.

main_text.p: Deus vero me hactenus custodivit, fecit-que ut intelligam haud mirum esse oportere, si homines Affectuum suorum Impotentiae relicti, vel multa ipsi mala faciant vel alio-rum Bonitate abutantur, cujus ingrata Nau-sea, Morbus omnium deploratissimus & In-sanabilis.

Haud tamen propterea liquido jam pof-sum affirmare, poenituisse me hujus consilii, cum in illud intuear non ut voluntatis meae crimen sed ut errorem Judicii in Charitatem impendio propensi. Id tantum dolet, aliorum oculos improbos factos, quia mei boni erant.

p.i: Te Domine semper appello, cujus omnia explo-rans Justitia per humana quaecunque velamina, & fallaces cordium tenebras clare penetrat.
Tu mihi cor dedisti ut haec subditis meis conce-derem, jam corde praeparato opus est, quo multa ab illis vicissim tolerem.
Fiat voluntas tua, nostrae quantumvis contrariæ[?], etiam tum cum speravimus & voluntati tuæ & eorum morem gerere, qui nil praeter tuam jactabant.
Erudiat me Gratia tua æquè frui Sapienter fru-strationibus his meis, ac sit spes meas optimas & speciosissima desideria explevisses.
Dum aliorum timoribus mederi cogitabam, meos auxi, & illos demum sedando meipsum tur-bavi.

page.notes: Bottom right number read as "194"; the last digit is doubtful and may be "184" or a damaged figure, so it is marked [?]. The word "contrariae" is marked [?] because the ligature is hard to read. The Latin passages are set in italic, and each sentence is printed as its own paragraph. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout. Running head is Greek and rendered with Greek letters as printed.
